key_insight: The paper introduces Q-DIBA, the first input-aware dynamic backdoor attack for quantum neural networks, showing that dynamic triggers can bypass weaknesses of fixed-trigger quantum backdoors.
engineering_relevance: This matters for quantum ML security because it reveals a practical attack path that can preserve clean accuracy while remaining stealthy against common defenses.
method: Uses a classical trigger generator jointly trained with a victim QNN.
Employs a three-mode mini-batch strategy for clean behavior, attack activation, and trigger specificity.
Adds an ensemble density contrastive loss on post-ansatz quantum states before measurement.
evidence_signal: Experiments on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST across multiple QNN architectures report high clean accuracy, strong attack success, high cross-trigger accuracy, and resilience to visual inspection, spectral-signature detection, and fine-tuning.
watch_item: The approach depends on training-time access to the victim QNN and careful quantum-state supervision, so its practicality may vary with device noise, model architecture, and deployment constraints.
paper_title: Input-Aware Dynamic Backdoor Attack Against Quantum Neural Networks
